newsitem.title: USA: Medical Industries says gets settlement.
newsitem.headline: Medical Industries says gets settlement.

text.p: Medical Industries of America Inc said Monday it will receive more than $1.1 million cash for a settlement of a legal dispute with offshore investors.
The company said it entered into a settlement agreement on April 7 with the plaintiffs of the Tula Business Inc, et al, lawsuit and certain other claimants.

The company said these plaintiffs, collectively, were suing for delivery of nearly nine million free trading common shares of the company, and the company was counter-suing the plaintiffs for claims that included market conditioning, malicious interference, extortion, Civil Rico violations, and market manipulation.
The company said the settlement provides that it issue a total of 2,063,346 free trading common shares to the plaintiffs.
The company said the plaintiffs agreed to exercise all outstanding warrants issued under the original rights offering, which have been converted into 144,384 common shares valued at $1.50 per share.

The company said that in addition to paying the company $216,576 for the conversion of these warrants, they paid an additional $900,000 in cash as settlement of the counter claims filed by the company.

The company said the plaintiffs and the claimants comprise a subset of the investors that participated in the company's securities offerings of Series C and Convertible Preferred Stock pursuant to Regulation S in February and March 1996.
